content.comment_body: Hello, I've built a system with a [product_name] controller from the 6th generation and a [product_name] display module. While my program worked in simulation, I encountered issues when running it on actual hardware. Specifically, using the directional arrows to increment a counter doesn't function as expected. Has anyone else faced similar problems? Thank you
Hi, [user_name] I can review your program. This may help: [url]

I had similar issues with the cursor keys on the controller module. I tried several suggestions, but none worked consistently. Ultimately, I resorted to using the standard inputs instead. Hopefully, this issue will be resolved in [version_no].
Hello Try pressing Esc and the Arrow key together.

To use the cursor key as an input, you need to press both the ESC key and the cursor key at the same time. This is necessary because the cursor keys are also used for navigating the controller's menu. The best approach is to go to the cursor key menu—accessed by pressing the left cursor while viewing the clock on the display. Then you’ll see the cursor symbol on the screen. Pressing ESC and the cursor key together will highlight the cursor symbol.
Thank you, I'll give that a try.
I tried your suggestion with Esc + arrow, but it only works intermittently. Is there a reliable solution for this problem? Thanks

I encountered the same issue, [user_name]. I've reviewed various forums and attempted all proposed solutions, but eventually switched to a separate input and switches. The functionality isn't consistent, as you mentioned—it only works sometimes. Hoping this is improved in [version_no]...

The source of the issue is timing. Pressing ESC too long before the cursor button sets the controller to the STOP menu, but pressing ESC too briefly also doesn't work. This timing challenge persists in [article_no], since both the ESC and arrow keys serve multiple functions, so the system distinguishes actions based on timing.

Hello, I’m not sure if others have discovered this, but I wanted to share. I struggled with using the directional arrows on the display module to increment a counter, but found something that works reliably. Normally, you should press Esc + arrow, but that isn’t efficient when repeated. Instead, press Esc + arrow, release both, then press OK. Repeat this process for each increment. Bye [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having trouble with inconsistent behavior when utilizing the directional/cursor arrows on [product_name] display modules for program control, such as incrementing counters. While simulation environments function correctly, real hardware often fails to respond reliably to the ESC + arrow key combination. Timing and overlapping button features complicate usage. Some users have tried various suggestions or given up, hoping future versions resolve the issue.
